decision: Blocking call identified: the dialog parks inside a coroutine dispatch driver, not in a plain callScript. DispatchDriver (game_type.cpp:3428-3452) starts a HostDispatch root, which calls VmScheduler::startHostTask; when the script waits, the scheduler thread parks (VmScheduler::wait sets waitingOn/flags 0x10 and yields) and DispatchDriver::resume only resumes it when context.pending->finished, i.e. after scheduler.tick + notify. So the host task 'host:handleEvent' is the ONLY place the click's Dialog.display() runs, and the notify that would finish it can only come from an osdCommand delivered through that same task -- a self-deadlock by construction, not a missing thread
why: Names the exact blocking call and why no separate dispatch thread helps by itself: the parked task owns both the wait and the only path that could notify it
evidence: threads.txt stack Dialog.display() @10/20 (op 08 = the wait invoke) under MainMenuDialog.osdCommand <- Gadget.sendMessage <- Button.click <- Group.handleEvent, all inside 'host:handleEvent [host task]' frozen at slices=337 f1005; game_type.cpp:3428-3452 DispatchDriver::resume; vm.cpp:3854-3875 VmScheduler::wait/notify

DispatchDriver::resume (3428-3452) only continues the coroutine when context.pending->finished, so the animation dispatch blocks until its subscriber's handleEvent host task finishes. That task is the one parked in Dialog.display()->wait(). The OK click that would call Dialog.osdCommand->notify can only be delivered by another pass of the same blocked coroutine -- a construction-level deadlock. CursorDispatch exists (4007-4049) but is constructed only by tests, never in production

Added a regression block that runs an awaited AnimationDispatch and asserts playerAnimationDelta is delivered, the scheduler ends idle and threadCount()==0
